Use Capivara to define regions by their spectra, measure their light, and explore
their spatial relationships. Start with a prepared cube and aligned quality and
variance arrays, as in [Analyse your own data](your-own-data.html).

## Choose what makes two spectra similar

The representation is a scientific choice, not a computational convenience.
Choose absolute flux when brightness is part of the question. Use a declared
spectral-shape representation when a positive multiplicative amplitude is a
nuisance. The MaNGA/Sandra profile has an instrument-specific validation domain;
it is not a universal normalizer for other surveys.

```{r workflow, eval=FALSE}
library(capivara)

seg <- segment_spectra(
  cube = cube,
  n_regions = 25L,
  representation = full_flux_representation(),
  variance = variance,
  sample_validity = valid
)

plot_regions(seg)
region_geometry(seg, coords = "native")
region_adjacency(seg, coords = "native")
```

The requested count is a cut through a hierarchy, not a count of physical
populations. The hierarchy can retain more regions if reliable comparisons
do not support further merges. See [Semantic representations](semantic-representations.html)
to choose a representation and inspect coverage.

## Extract the spectra you want to fit

The extraction function preserves the existing summary object. If you have a
quality mask, explicitly apply it to a copy of the retained cube before
extraction. Channels with missing contributors are not fixed-aperture sums.

```{r extraction, eval=FALSE}
quality_seg <- seg
quality_seg$original_cube$imDat[!valid] <- NA_real_
spectra <- extract_region_spectra(quality_seg, variance = variance)

fixed <- spectra$sum_spectra
complete <- sweep(spectra$finite_counts, 1L, spectra$n_spaxels, "==")
fixed[!complete] <- NA_real_
```

The returned variance summaries assume diagonal errors, with an optional scalar
inflation. They do not propagate a full spatial or spectral covariance model.

For a legacy cube with suitable FITS axis metadata,
`plot_region_spectra(seg)` displays individual median-centred profiles
and the region median; it is not a plot of calibrated summed flux.

Use `list_emission_lines()` to inspect the laboratory line registry before
constructing line-sensitive analyses. The registry itself is not a line fit.

## Existing scripts still work

The regional interfaces complement the original functions. No historical call
or scientific default has changed.

| To do this | Regional interface | Existing interface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Segment with an explicit representation | `segment_spectra()` | `segment_large()` or `segment()` with a declaration |
| Extract spectra | `extract_region_spectra()` | `summarize_cluster_spectra()` |
| Draw a region map | `plot_regions()` | `plot_cluster()` |
| Display scaled profiles | `plot_region_spectra()` | `plot_cluster_spectra()` |
| Inspect polygons | `region_geometry()` | `regions_sf()` |
| List laboratory lines | `list_emission_lines()` | `emission_lines()` |

The new segmentation interface always selects the explicit observed-entry
spatial hierarchy. For historical exact or sparse feature-graph segmentation,
and for the existing target-S/N cutting options, continue using the original
interfaces. They are not interchangeable with the new scientific representation.

See the [function reference](../reference/index.html) for advanced controls,
kinematics, reconstruction, spatial contracts and export functions.
